mission: Investigate how secure the emerging agent economy really is, using public evidence only, and publish what holds up.
open_questions: The operator review queue is now 10 items deep (seq 58-67), unresolved since wake125/wake116 for many wakes running -- this wake's own new piece will likely add an 11th once classify's named_org_negative_claim flag routes it there. Worth confirming next wake whether staging/wake140-entra-agent-id-blocked-permissions-gap.md queued as expected.

Compass Security's privilege-equivalence classification for the six permissions (that they carry genuinely equivalent impact to their blocked siblings) was not independently re-derived from Microsoft's Graph permissions reference this wake -- if a future wake wants to strengthen this finding, reading the individual permission definitions in Microsoft's Graph permissions reference and confirming what each one actually grants would let a future piece make that claim directly rather than by attribution.

Whether Microsoft has any changelog, GitHub PR, or advisory tracking the Compass-reported gap (the Compass post links a PR for an unrelated documentation gap -- the missing Security Reader role -- but not for the blocked-permissions gap) is unknown; a search for one wasn't done this wake.

Tooling reminders: export PATH=/workspace/tools:$PATH before secre-record. secre-record payload must NOT include top-level 'kind', 'wake', or 'prev_hash' keys. Ledger files are decision_log.jsonl, claims_ledger.jsonl, evidence_ledger.jsonl under /memory/ledgers/ -- evidence_ledger is auto-populated by secre-fetch itself (each fetch appends a proxy_tunnel record), no manual evidence recording needed. harness.publish.Publication.load needs a Path not a str; loaded object's category field is declared_categories. harness.secrets_scan.scan/classify.classify take text (pub.body), not the Publication object. harness.citations.validate is a function -- import as 'from harness.citations import validate as cv' and call cv(text, ledger, exempt_hosts=[...]). Its Ledger is constructed as harness.ledger.Ledger(path) directly (a plain constructor) -- there is no Ledger.load classmethod, that call fails with AttributeError. Always run this pipeline check before staging, not after.
